name: next_steps
title: Next Steps
description: Every concrete commitment agreed on the call — which side owns it, what kind of step it is, how firm the commitment sounded (judged by the actual words), and the spoken due date verbatim.
prompt:
List every concrete next step actually agreed or promised on this call — one entry per action. A vague intention ("we should look into that sometime") is not a next step. An empty list is correct when nothing was agreed.

For each next step:
- evidence: cite the utterance(s) where the action is agreed or promised, before you write "text". The words that fix the type and commitment reads below (a date, a hedge, a firm yes) must be among the quotes you cite here.
- text: the action, stated from the owner's side, <=240 characters. Quote the speaker's exact words for what was promised wherever a direct quote exists — no number-word/digit conversion.
- type: the kind of step, judged by the quote. concrete_date = a specific date, day, or deadline is named ("Friday", "next Tuesday", "by the 15th"); send_info = a promise to send material, a link, a quote, or a document; soft_followup = a vague agreement to reconnect with no date ("let's touch base", "circle back"); no_next_step = the parties explicitly agreed on nothing further. Use "unclear" when none clearly fits.
- owner: which side owns the action — rep, buyer, joint only when both explicitly share it, else unknown. Never guess an owner the transcript does not support.
- commitment: how firm it sounded, judged by the modal words in the quote. firm = an unhedged commitment or a named date ("I will send it Friday", "yes, we'll do that"); tentative = hedged with a modal or condition ("probably", "might", "let me check", "if I can"). Use "unclear" when the words do not settle it. Do not upgrade a hedge to firm because the deal feels positive.
- due: the spoken timeframe copied verbatim ("by friday", "next quarter"). Use an empty string when no timeframe was spoken — never invent one.
